provider_query: Python standard library documentation for the venv module
answer:
Official and closely related documentation for Python’s standard-library `venv` module:

1. **venv — Creation of virtual environments (Python 3.14 library reference)** — Primary stdlib docs: purpose, `python -m venv`, CLI flags (`--system-site-packages`, `--clear`, `--upgrade`, `--without-pip`, etc.), and the `EnvBuilder` API. Added in 3.3; source under `Lib/venv/`.  
   https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/venv.html  
   [[1]](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/venv.html)

2. **Same library page (stable index via search)** — Same reference, current stable docs.python.org entry for `venv`.  
   https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/venv.html  
   [[1]](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/venv.html)

3. **Tutorial: Virtual Environments and Packages (Python 3.13)** — How-to: create with `python -m venv`, common `.venv` layout, activate on Windows vs Unix/macOS, and what activation changes (`PATH`, prompt, `sys.path`).  
   https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/venv.html  
   [[2]](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/venv.html)

4. **Tutorial source (dev / 3.15 alpha)** — Same tutorial chapter on the development docs.  
   https://docs.python.org/dev/tutorial/venv.html  
   [[3]](https://docs.python.org/dev/tutorial/venv.html)

5. **CPython tutorial RST (GitHub raw)** — Upstream reStructuredText for the tutorial chapter (`Doc/tutorial/venv.rst`).  
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/HEAD/Doc/tutorial/venv.rst  
   [[4]](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/HEAD/Doc/tutorial/venv.rst)

6. **pydevtools handbook — venv** — Practical summary of the stdlib module (since 3.3), comparison with virtualenv/uv, flags such as `--upgrade-deps`, and that `pyvenv` was removed in 3.8.  
   https://pydevtools.com/handbook/reference/venv/  
   [[5]](https://pydevtools.com/handbook/reference/venv/)

7. **Python Land — create, activate, deactivate, delete** — Walkthrough of `python -m venv`, typical directory layout (`pyvenv.cfg`, `Scripts`/`bin`, `site-packages`), with a link out to the official docs.  
   https://python.land/virtual-environments/virtualenv  
   [[6]](https://python.land/virtual-environments/virtualenv)

8. **ZetCode — Python venv** — Short guide: create/activate on Linux and Windows, and what `pyvenv.cfg` and `site-packages` are for.  
   https://zetcode.com/python/venv/  
   [[7]](https://zetcode.com/python/venv/)

**Core usage (from the official library page):** `python -m venv /path/to/env` creates an isolated environment on top of the invoking interpreter; activate with `source path/bin/activate` (Unix/macOS) or `path\Scripts\activate` (Windows).
